column1: # Real return ASYMMETRY: the three statistics behind the `downside/upside vol` and `leverage
# asymmetry` fidelity rows, which AsymmetryAnchorSuite / asymmetry_anchor_tests re-derive from
# this file. Editing a row moves the shipped anchors. Nothing else is fitted from this file.
# All three are uni.apps.MarketSim's own definitions, close-only daily log returns:
#   sdRatio  sqrt(sum(r^2 | r<0) / sum(r^2 | r>0)), tau = 0 (Roy 1952 / Markowitz 1959 ch.9)
#   betaN/betaP  OLS of next-block realized variance on this block's SIGNED halves
#            RS- = sum(r^2 | r<0), RS+ = sum(r^2 | r>0), RV_{t+1} ~ RS-_t + RS+_t, demeaned
#   levAsym  (betaN - betaP) / (betaN + betaP): 0 = sign-blind clustering, 1 = downside does
#            all the forecasting (betaP = 0), above 1 = betaP negative
#   levCorr  corr(r_t, r^2_{t+1}), the classic daily leverage correlation (supporting column)
# WHAT THIS FILE SETTLES. Volatility clustering (|r|) and the variance-ratio row are both blind
# to WHICH SIGN carries the dispersion and the persistence. Three findings, two usable:
#   - sdRatio: downside exceeds upside on every CRSP era (1.028-1.031, stable to the third
#     digit) and on 15 of 18 full-history funds (0.986-1.061). The EXCESS is what a row can
#     grade -- the ratio itself sits so near 1 that a model/real quotient could never miss.
#   - levCorr: negative on all 18 funds (-0.17..-0.03) and stable on every CRSP era
#     (-0.092/-0.093/-0.100). This is the anchorable leverage statistic.
#   - betaN/betaP CANNOT ANCHOR, and the columns are committed so that stays settled: the
#     century flips the sign (levAsym c1926 -0.20, c1954 -0.15, c1990 +0.34 -- the 1930s' giant
#     up-days sit inside the same high-volatility stretches as the down-days), and the modern
#     cross-section spans -0.64..+1.82. The close-only 22-session block regression is not the
#     intraday statistic Patton & Sheppard read, and it does not inherit their conclusion.
# Measured 2026-08-31, fund data through 2026-08-20, CRSP through 2026-06-30.
#   w2001  2001-08-27.. -- the depth cross-section's window (opens mid-bear; fine here, these
#   c1926/c1954/c1990  CRSP value-weighted US market total return (Mkt-RF + RF), daily, from
#          Ken French's F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily, window opening in that year
